quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: You should leave extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they only have one tail light.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front moves to the right to let you pass.
The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side of the road is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side of the road is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for trains coming from either direction.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at crossings, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: As a vehicle's speed increases, stopping distances and collision severity:

options.text: Decrease.
Stay the same.
Increase.

questions.explanation: Speed greatly affects safety. As speed increases, the danger of a crash gets worse. Faster crashes cause more serious injuries and deaths. Leave more space between your vehicle and others as you go faster so you can stop safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Yield the right-of-way.
No passing zone.
Reduction in lanes.

questions.explanation: A red and white triangular sign means you must yield the right-of-way to other traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: Higher speeds increase the chance of a fatal crash.
As speed increases, you should leave more space between vehicles.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. Above 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is unlikely. Faster speeds require longer stopping distances, so increase your following distance as you speed up.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic away from hazardous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic away from hazardous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. These warn you of danger ahead.

questions.question: You can drive off the road to pass another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Your car can hydroplane in water at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when water pools on the road. Most tires can move water away at speeds up to 35 mph. Above 35 mph, tires lose contact with the road and ride over the water like skis.

questions.question: Collisions are more likely when:

options.text: All vehicles travel at about the same speed.
One lane travels faster than other lanes.
One vehicle travels faster or slower than the rest of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: One vehicle travels faster or slower than the rest of traffic.
questions.explanation: Collisions happen more often when a driver goes faster or slower than other vehicles. Driving faster than traffic increases crash risk. Driving slower than traffic also causes crashes because other drivers may hit you or swerve to avoid you.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can you have and still drive safely?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.explanation: You should not drive after drinking any alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: How far before turning should you use your turn signal?

options.text: 50 feet
75 feet
25 feet

questions.explanation: You must turn on your turn signal at least 50 feet before you turn.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, how fast should you drive?

options.text: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
At the legal speed limit.
More slowly than the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is going faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: You and another driver reach a four-way stop at the same time. The other driver is on your left. Who goes first?

options.text: The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
You have the right-of-way.
Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: Intersection.
Road curve.
Right turn.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns you that another road crosses the highway ahead.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop quickly. If you follow too closely, you will not have enough time to avoid a crash if the motorcycle stops suddenly.

questions.question: What should you do before passing on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming vehicles are moving. Always make sure you have enough space to pass safely. If you are unsure, wait until the oncoming vehicle passes before you pass.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing a vehicle?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, return to your original lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?

options.text: Service sign.
Regulatory sign.
Warning sign.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead, such as sharp curves, steep hills, or other hazards that require you to take action.

questions.question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Look toward the right edge of the road.
Switch your lights to high beams.
Turn your lights on and off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are blinding you, look toward the right edge of the road instead of ahead. This keeps your vehicle safe until you pass the oncoming vehicle.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, you must:

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. On one-way streets, drive toward the nearest edge.

questions.question: When driving in a construction zone:

options.text: Drive a little faster.
Be prepared for anything.
Expect workers to get out of your way.

questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected conditions. Drive with extra caution to keep yourself, other drivers, and workers safe.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Keep your speed to get through the water.
Stay away from the puddle if you can.
Shift into neutral as you drive through it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay away from the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. Dry, solid surfaces are the safest for driving.

questions.question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?

options.text: Never.
When you can see clearly in both directions.
When the warning lights are not flashing.

questions.explanation: Never go around or under a lowered gate at a railroad crossing. After the gate is raised, only cross the tracks when you can see clearly in both directions and know no trains are coming.

questions.question: If you have an argument with another person and are angry, you should:

options.text: Play loud music while driving so you won't think about it.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to feel better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Your emotions affect how safely you drive. If you are angry, excited, afraid, worried, or sad, take time to calm down before driving. You need to focus on the road.

questions.question: You are approaching a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter the intersection to claim your right-of-way.
Don't enter until you can drive all the way across.
Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't enter until you can drive all the way across.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, only enter an intersection if you can get completely across before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: On a multilane road, a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: No one can pass.
Everyone can pass.
Only cars next to the dashed line can pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only cars next to the dashed line can pass.
questions.explanation: When there is a solid line and a dashed line between lanes, only drivers next to the dashed line can cross to pass. Drivers next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: A broken yellow line between two lanes of traffic means:

options.text: Both lanes go in the same direction.
Passing is allowed when safe.
Passing is not allowed.

questions.explanation: Dashed yellow lines divide lanes moving in opposite directions. You can pass when there is no oncoming traffic in the passing lane.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a parked position at the curb, you:

options.text: Should drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Should wait for a gap large enough to match traffic speed.
Should wait for two vehicles to pass, then enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wait for a gap large enough to match traffic speed.
questions.explanation: When merging into traffic, wait for a gap large enough so your vehicle can reach the same speed as other traffic.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlights.
Use your parking lights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you, making it harder to see.
